the model says the meaning changed: The judge review step now runs as a subprocess of the worktree's own iaso source instead of the main checkout's in-process debug, which changes how the review the requirement relies on (EX-1, EX-2, EX-3, EX-5) is performed and how its failures are reported.; brought to the owner as a card: The requirement still matches what you asked for: iaso fixes itself in a separate worktree, the judge reviews the fix, and nothing is committed until the review passes. So the requirement doesn't need rewording.

What changed is how the review runs. It used to run inside the iaso that is doing the work, which is the copy in your main checkout. That copy still has the old code the fix replaces. Now the review runs as a separate `iaso debug` process on the worktree's own copy of the code, so the fixed code reviews itself. This looks like it supports your goal: before, a refusal the fix had rewritten would still come back unchanged. It also leaves your main checkout alone, as EX-6 requires.

There's one side effect you haven't approved. If that separate review process can't start or its output can't be read, the round now counts as a failed round. EX-5 instead says to hold and say so once when no judge can be reached. Each such round also counts toward the three-round limit, so a review that keeps failing to start could end the case as a defect report without a real review ever happening.
